newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Dalai Lama to visit Taiwan on March 22 - report.
newsitem.headline: Dalai Lama to visit Taiwan on March 22 - report.

text.p: The Dalai Lama, Tibetan Buddhism's exiled god-king, would start his six-day Taiwan visit on March 22, uninterrupted by the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, a Taipei newspaper reported on Sunday.
He could meet President Lee Teng-hui during his stay, the mass circulation United Daily News newspaper reported.
The host of the visit, Taiwan's Buddhist Association of the Republic of China, said it had consulted Lee's office for the meeting, but no date had been finalised,
Beijing considers the Dalai Lama and Lee as two leading "splittists" who seek to divide Tibet and Taiwan from the motherland and the reported meeting was almost certain to risk the wrath of China.
The Dalai Lama has voiced regret that Deng died without resolving questions over Tibet.

"Deng Xiaoping had been involved in the Tibetan issue from the very beginning, all the way through right up to the end, so it seems he had the intention to resolve the Tibetan issue himself during his own lifetime," the Dalai Lama said in an interview with the Tibetan service of Voice of America radio on Feburary 19.

Local media has reported the Dalai Lama would also meet high-level Taiwan officials during his stay, although the Taiwan host repeated the Tibetan god-king would have no official contacts and activities while in Taiwan.

China assails the Dalai Lama, who fled into exile in India in 1959 as a "splittist" seeking to divide Tibet from China and accuses countries that allow him to visit of meddling in China's internal affairs.

Similarly, China regards Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949. It views Lee's reforms, including direct presidential election in March 1996 and pursuit of international recognitions as moves for Taiwan independence.
The Dalai Lama has praised President Lee for initiating democratic reforms on the Nationalist island and Lee was reported to have welcomed the Dalai Lama to Taiwan in a May 1996 exchange of letters.
